event: "Okay, might just hunt my own then."
Marda grunts and goes back to her ledger.
At the Crook and Candle Nala eats a bowl of stew with bread for 3 copper and takes a bed for 8.
She sleeps hard and wakes in the gray before first light, whole, her well brimming.
At first light two folk wait on Brannagh's bench.
An old shepherd off the slate rolls up his trouser. A ram's-horn scar runs down his shin.
Her first Mending slides off the old scar tissue. The mana goes, and nothing changes.
The next three take. The ridge flattens, pales, and goes smooth.
The shepherd runs his thumb down his shin. He says nothing and leaves a wedge of hill cheese.
The second is a woodcutter with yesterday's axe gash in his shin. It's clean, with no blight in it.
One weave closes it. He counts 10 copper into her hand.
She reaches the south green late. The watch is already on laps, and Maud jerks her chin at the line.
Laps, then hauling fieldstone until her arms shake.
Then staff bouts with Tam. She slips his swing and raps his knuckles. He swears, then grins.
She stays until the watch changes, near half past ten.
At the Post, Marda looks up. "Two leads came in."
"The blighted boar's track crossed the south road by Edda Crane's clearing."
"Level fourteen. A silver fifty on the board. It ranges between the road and the Wren Brook ford."
"And a woodcutter found a deer by the Wren Brook, its hide rotted to black sludge."
"Small blight first, I'd say." Marda taps the board. "But it's your hunt."
